# Mathematical foundations

The mathematical sequence develops fields and linear algebra, calculus and
surface geometry, function spaces, differential equations, Fourier analysis,
spherical harmonics, and numerical projection. Probability and integral operators
then connect physical averages to learned maps.

These chapters share their source with the
[mathematical-prerequisites companion](https://github.com/tglanz/climatology/blob/main/presentations/mathematical-prerequisites/mathematical-prerequisites.md),
which also supplies a linked PDF, chapter summaries, self-tests, and answers.
Arfken and Weber's sixth edition, abbreviated AW, is the principal source @ArfkenWeber2005;
Hunter defines the weak-solution notation @HunterPDE, and NIST gives the explicit
Gaussian quadrature rule @NISTDLMFQuadrature.

Equations prefixed **M** retain the companion's chapter-equation numbers, independently
of the book's chapter order. Equations prefixed **P** belong to the physical
companion. Guide chapter numbers in plural cross-references refer to the companion;
linked concept names refer to their owning book chapter. The mathematical
companion's fluid application is represented here by the more detailed
[fluid-dynamics sequence](../04-geophysical-fluid-dynamics/index.qmd).

The mathematical chapters use colatitude $\theta$, latitude $\varphi$, longitude
$\lambda$, physical radius $R$, and $d\Omega=dA/R^2$. Some fluid chapters write
latitude as $\phi$ and solid angle as $d\omega$; these denote the same geometric
quantities. Inner products are linear in the first argument. Fourier series
use normalized measure $dx/d$ on a period $d$; the whole-line transform uses
angular wavenumber $k$ and inverse factor $1/(2\pi)$. Every transform and physical
average states its measure explicitly.
